root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `Parser::makeStream()` clears the `Parsing` flag, its cached `entry` pointer must still be the live xref slot for `objNum`; if `dictLookup("Length", recursion)` reconstructed the xref, `entry` must be refreshed from `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` before the clear call executes.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable run reaches the cleanup clear with `entry` still naming the pre-reconstruction slot while `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` names the rebuilt slot, so the required equality is violated exactly where the sanitizer trace locates the root cause. In the fixed run the refreshed `entry` matches the live slot before `setFlag` executes.

nodes.state: `XRefEntry::setFlag()` receives the same `XRefEntry *` through `this` and performs the ASan-reported read-modify-write of `flags` at the sink.
`XRef::constructXRef()` frees the current `entries` heap array with `gfree(entries)`, invalidating any cached `XRefEntry *` that still points into that array.

edges.relation: The `entry` pointer observed at `Parser::makeStream()` cleanup is passed unchanged into `XRefEntry::setFlag()` as `this`, carrying the stale slot to the sanitizer sink.

The same `entries` array base freed during xref reconstruction is the array base recovered from the cached `entry` at cleanup, proving the later clear runs after the free on the same xref-entry storage.
